description: Changes a keyword. You can rename it with term: the new term is tracked from now on, with no look-back, and the keyword keeps its id, settings and what the old term found. You can set its platforms (a list, or null for all), mute or unmute it, change its kind, or set its classifier context (null clears it). You can change its matching rules, where each field is optional and an empty list clears it, with requiredTerms and requiredMode any or all, excludedTerms with a `*` wildcard at either end, excludedAuthors and caseSensitive. You can set its monthly cap with cap: { mentions: N }, where null removes it and a cap above this month's count resumes a capped keyword right away. You can move it with groupId, which returns 409 if that group already has the term. You can set reviewSources, the full list of App Store, Google Play, Trustpilot or Google Maps pages, where an empty list disconnects them and a newly added app or country brings its last 30 days free. You can replace the RSS or Atom feeds it reads with feeds, the whole list of { url }, where an empty list disconnects them and a newly added feed brings its newest 10 matching items of the last 30 days. You can switch comments on or off with comments ({ enabled, maxPerPost }; $0.008 per comment delivered). Rules only affect new mentions. Returns the keyword after the change, with its stats.

inputSchema.description: Fields you leave out stay as they are.

anyOf.description: The most mentions this keyword can match per month. At the cap it stops matching until the 1st of next month (UTC), or until the cap is raised or removed. It is not muted, so its daily charge continues. Mute it to stop that as well.

mentions.description: How many matched mentions the keyword may collect per calendar month (UTC). Every match counts, relevant or not, including a new keyword's look-back, since every match is billed.

cap.description: Sets a new monthly mention cap, or null for no cap. A cap above this month's count resumes a capped keyword right away. A cap at or below the count pauses it.

comments.description: Comments under this keyword's mentions; omitted fields stay as they are (on create: off, 20 per mention).

enabled.description: Read the comments under this keyword's relevant mentions, from 30 minutes after each post, while its platform's conversations last. Each comment delivered costs $0.008 on the comments line of the bill (comments of fewer than three words are dropped, never billed). Off by default.

maxPerPost.description: How many of a thread's newest comments you receive, 20 by default and 100 at most: the ceiling on what one mention's comments can cost. A comment that names the keyword is a mention too, but only among these.

anyOf.description: Up to 300 characters the classifier reads for this keyword only, in addition to the company profile or the group's description. Say what the term means for you and what to ignore, for example "Basil is our deploy tool, not the herb." Null clears it.

context.description: Up to 300 characters the classifier reads for this keyword only, in addition to the company profile or the group's description. Say what the term means for you and what to ignore, for example "Basil is our deploy tool, not the herb." Null clears it.

feeds.description: RSS or Atom feeds this keyword reads, at most 20, each { url }: a feed's address, or a page's (a forum, a community, a blog), whose advertised feed is used, else a usual address such as /feed or /rss. Every feed is checked when saved, and a 400 names each one that cannot be read and why. Feeds are read every hour; an item is a mention of this keyword when it holds the term (with its matching rules), and only of keywords that named the feed. A newly connected feed brings its newest 10 matching items of the last 30 days, billed like any mention. On PATCH the list replaces the old one, and [] disconnects them all (their mentions stay).

url.description: A feed's address (https://forum.example.com/posts.rss), or a page's (https://forum.example.com), whose advertised feed is used.

groupId.description: Target group (grp_...). 409 if it already has this term.

matching.description: Fields you leave out stay as they are. An empty list clears a field.

caseSensitive.description: When true, the term only matches in the exact case you typed, so RAG never matches rag. Defaults to false.

excludedAuthors.description: Authors whose posts this keyword ignores. Each entry is a profile or post link, @handle, u/name, Bluesky DID or display name. Entries are normalized the same way as an alert's muted authors.

excludedTerms.description: Posts that contain one of these terms are dropped. Put `*` at the start or end of a term as a wildcard, so deploy* matches deployment and *bot matches nightlybot.

requiredMode.description: any needs one of the required terms in the post. all needs every one.

requiredTerms.description: Terms the post must contain as well. requiredMode says whether one or all of them must appear. An empty list sets no requirement.

muted.description: Muting stops polling and matching. Existing mentions are kept.

platforms.description: Sets a new platform list. Null means all platforms. An empty list means none, which works when the keyword has reviewSources and only collects reviews.

reviewSources.description: Sets a new list of review pages for this keyword. An empty list disconnects them all, and their reviews are kept. A page or country you add gets the free 30-day look-back. Pages already listed are unchanged.

items.description: A review page, by link or by platform and id. Its reviews become this keyword's mentions.

countries.description: For App Store and Google Play. Up to 20 storefronts to read, as two-letter codes. Without it, the storefront in the link is used, or us. Each storefront adds one poll a day, and a review found in two storefronts is still one mention. Trustpilot and Google Maps have a single page and take no countries.

id.description: The platform's own id. On the App Store it is the number after "id" in the link, on Google Play the package name, on Trustpilot the company's domain (slack.com) and on Google Maps a Place ID (ChIJ...).

language.description: For Google Play. The review language to read, such as en, es, de or pt-BR, since Google Play returns one language at a time. Without it, the link's hl is used, or en.

platform.description: Where the reviews come from. appstore is the Apple App Store, googleplay is Google Play, trustpilot is a company's Trustpilot page and googlemaps is the Google reviews of a place.

url.description: Review page link, or send platform and id instead. Accepts App Store and Google Play app links (https://apps.apple.com/us/app/slack/id618783545, https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.Slack), Trustpilot pages (https://www.trustpilot.com/review/slack.com) and Google Maps places (full or maps.app.goo.gl link).

term.description: A new term for the keyword. It keeps its id, settings and the mentions the old term found, and the new term is tracked from now on, with no look-back. A 409 when its group already tracks the new term.
